stories.title: India faces $6.5 trillion funding gap for net-zero goal
stories.summary: A report by economist Nicki Hutley estimates India requires $22.7 trillion to reach net-zero emissions by 2070. While domestic resources may cover 70 percent of the investment, a $6.5 trillion funding gap remains. International capital is described as crucial to achieving the country's climate and development goals.

stories.summary: New Delhi: India’s ambition to achieve net-zero emissions by 2070 could create an estimated USD 22.7 trillion investment opportunity across clean energy and infrastructure, but mobilising that capital will require substantial international funding, according to a report by Australian economist Nicki Hutley. stories.title: Solvent-free laminates market shifts toward mainstream
stories.summary: The global solvent-free laminates market is transitioning from a compliance-driven niche to a mainstream specification for furniture and construction. IndexBox reports that demand through 2035 will be supported by tightening volatile organic compound regulations in North America and Europe. The market is currently adopting more disciplined procurement behavior.

stories.title: Mineral ceiling tiles market expands with construction cycles
stories.summary: The global mineral ceiling tiles market is entering a phase of steady expansion, according to IndexBox. The sector is shaped by regulatory tightening and evolving facility standards. Tiles are increasingly specified for acoustic and fire-resistant properties, as the industry moves toward a more regionally diversified supply architecture.

stories.title: Foster + Partners completes kinetic observatory dome
stories.summary: Foster + Partners has unveiled a 20-meter-diameter observatory dome at the Ellison Institute of Technology in Oxford. The structure features a moving steel exoskeleton that tracks the sun to adjust its position. It is described as a kinetic structure that converts solar motion into a legible mark.

stories.title: Solar cooling reduces emissions in Qatari buildings
stories.summary: A study in Green Technology, Resilience, and Sustainability suggests that combining Passivhaus-level insulation with solar cooling can reduce carbon dioxide emissions in Qatari agro-industrial communities. The research modeled residential and greenhouse structures to quantify how improved thermal efficiency might offset high energy demands for air conditioning in arid climates.

stories.title: Continuous insulation market projected to reach $67.74 billion
stories.summary: MarketsandMarkets projects the global continuous insulation market will grow from $56.98 billion in 2026 to $67.74 billion by 2031. The sector is expected to maintain a compound annual growth rate of 3.5 percent over the five-year forecast period as it tracks global construction trends.

stories.title: NSE unveils design for new Mumbai headquarters
stories.summary: The National Stock Exchange has revealed architectural renderings for a new headquarters in Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex. Designed by Hafeez Contractor, the building features an angular structure with an upper mass that tilts outwards. The exchange describes the project as a landmark intended to reflect innovation and ambition.

stories.title: AM/NS India begins work on $70,000 crore steel plant
stories.summary: AM/NS India has laid the foundation for an integrated steel plant in Andhra Pradesh with a planned investment of 70,000 crore rupees. The facility aims for an initial capacity of 8.2 million tonnes. It is the first greenfield steel plant to be started in India in nearly a decade.

stories.title: Oshinówò Studio adds glass prism to Lutyens war memorial
stories.summary: The Commonwealth War Graves Commission has unveiled a memorial to the Sierra Leone Carrier Corps in Freetown. Designed by Oshinówò Studio, the glass structure sits atop a 1931 Lutyens memorial that previously omitted the 946 men who died while transporting supplies during the first world war.

stories.title: Fala Atelier completes Cookie Cutter Retreat in Portugal
stories.summary: Porto studio Fala Atelier has embedded three semicircular concrete volumes into a Portuguese hillside for a digital nomad retreat. The buildings feature blue chimneys and grass roofs, which the architects claim almost disappear into the landscape. The project includes a private house, a shared dwelling and a hall.

stories.title: Architect completes Minimal Maximum House in Prague
stories.summary: Jan Jakub Tesař of Stempel and Tesar has finished a 70 square meter family home in Prague. Described as a personal manifesto condensing two decades of residential design experience, the house uses interlocking floors to maximize space on a tight urban plot. It is a highly concentrated response.

stories.title: Simple Architecture renovates 1960s Zagreb apartment
stories.summary: Simple Architecture has renovated an apartment in a 1960s New Zagreb residential block. The project involved stripping the interior back to its raw concrete shell, utilizing the building's original prefabricated modular system. The renovation focused on subtraction to reveal the raw state of the structure.

stories.title: Center for Architecture exhibits work of the Nowickis
stories.summary: The Center for Architecture in New York is hosting an exhibition on Stanisława Sandecka-Nowicka and Maciej Nowicki. Curated by Kacper Kępiński, the show presents the pair as equal partners in their architectural work. It is the first exhibition to focus on their shared body of work.

stories.title: Book explores Mesoamerican modern architecture
stories.summary: Curator Su Wu has released a book detailing five examples of contemporary Mexican homes that reinterpret ancient architectural principles. Wu chose the term Mesoamerican Modern to highlight that the logic of pre-Columbian monumentalism did not end. The projects focus on residential architecture from the 1970s to today.

stories.title: Mexico sees architecture renaissance inspired by ancient past
stories.summary: A new generation of Mexican architects is creating private residences that reinterpret ancient siting principles and geometries. Curator Su Wu argues these homes reflect complex aesthetic cultures, moving away from the term pre-Columbian to emphasize that these ancient architectural logics remain a living part of contemporary design.

stories.title: SpY installs black triangle in Madrid
stories.summary: Artist SpY has placed a 20-meter matte-black triangle in Madrid's Plaza de Cibeles. The temporary structure uses concealed apertures and live CCTV feeds to monitor the public square. The installation is intended to reverse the relationship between the watcher and the watched by interrupting local sightlines.

stories.title: Rotterdam architecture biennale occupies industrial site
stories.summary: The 12th International Architecture Biennale Rotterdam is currently held in the abandoned De Piekfabriek halls. The exhibition, titled Systems Of Support, explores how design addresses spatial and ecological challenges. The surrounding Feijenoord area is slated for transformation based on a masterplan by local practice KCAP.

stories.title: Bancroft begins mass timber project in New Jersey
stories.summary: Bancroft Construction is redeveloping the Wetlands Institute campus in Stone Harbor, New Jersey, using mass timber. The project includes an 18,640-square-foot elevated building designed to support research and community programming. It is the company's first mass timber project, intended to address the challenges of a coastal location.

stories.title: Industry experts gather for mass timber event in Providence
stories.summary: Shawmut Design and Construction hosted a mass timber event in Providence on November 5. Alongside WSP and Nordic Structures, the firm convened over 100 industry partners to discuss the material's expanding role in U.S. construction. The event focused on project delivery decisions and the benefits of mass timber.

stories.title: Mercer International reports negative EBITDA for solid-wood
stories.summary: Mercer International's solid-wood segment reported negative US$7 million in operating EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026. Despite the loss, the company noted a mass-timber order book of approximately US$151 million. The segment's revenue reached US$128.6 million during the same period.

stories.title: U.S. Army tests 3D-printed facade panels
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is testing 3D-printed facade panels for use in energy-efficient building renovations. The project aims to improve the thermal performance of existing structures through additive manufacturing. Further details on the testing results are available in the full piece for subscribers.

stories.title: Coal mine waste used to create load-bearing bricks
stories.summary: Researchers in India have developed a method to manufacture load-bearing bricks using 100 percent overburden waste sand from coal mines. The process eliminates the need for cement or fired clay. The study claims the material performs as well as traditional masonry while reducing construction carbon emissions.

stories.title: 3D-printed engine runs briefly
stories.summary: A 3D-printed engine has been constructed and successfully operated, though its performance was limited. The project highlights the challenges of using plastic materials in high-heat environments, given that most 3D-printing filaments have melting points significantly lower than the temperatures found inside a running internal combustion engine.

stories.title: 3D-printed tungsten tiles survive fusion machine test
stories.summary: Researchers from North Carolina State University and Oak Ridge National Laboratory 3D-printed tungsten tiles for a fusion machine. The tiles survived 74 plasma blasts, remaining intact even after a neighboring tile melted. Tungsten is favored for fusion reactors due to its high melting point, though it is difficult to shape.

stories.title: Northwestern researchers develop DIAL 3D printing
stories.summary: Researchers at Northwestern University have developed direct ink additive lithography, a hybrid process for printing thick, functional inks. The method combines ink sheet extrusion with a moving projector to achieve speeds and resolutions similar to light-based printing. The findings were published in the journal Science Advances.

stories.title: Materialise reports productivity gains on EOS printer
stories.summary: Materialise has trialed an upcoming EOS polymer 3D printing platform, reporting 44 percent higher throughput compared to previous systems. The new technology is scheduled for a full launch on November 17 at Formnext 2026. The trial also showed a reduction in build time per part.

stories.title: Agra air quality dips after Diwali
stories.summary: Air quality in Agra deteriorated following Diwali, with sensors at two locations recording an AQI above 400. While the Central Pollution Control Board reported a city-wide average of 190, local monitoring sensors indicated severe pollution levels across several districts. The air is currently choosing its own metrics.

stories.title: Delhi invokes Stage III pollution curbs
stories.summary: Delhi’s 24-hour average Air Quality Index reached 376 on Sunday, placing the city in the very poor category. The Commission for Air Quality Management invoked Stage III of its Graded Response Action Plan on November 6. The city is now managing its air through administrative stages.

stories.title: Srinagar urban growth impacts wetlands
stories.summary: A study in the journal City and Built Environment documents Srinagar’s expansion from 1992 to 2024. Researchers found that rapid urban growth occurred at the direct expense of ecologically sensitive wetlands and agricultural lands. The city has successfully traded its natural buffers for a higher heat index.

stories.title: Study suggests six-acre parks cool cities
stories.summary: A 2026 study suggests that Bengaluru’s parks provide cooling effects that extend hundreds of metres beyond their boundaries. Researchers identified 2.49 hectares, or roughly six acres, as a target size for effective urban planning. Concrete is finally being asked to consider the shade.

stories.title: Mathura and Vrindavan plan four-lane corridor
stories.summary: The Mathura-Vrindavan Development Authority plans a 12-km four-lane road along an old railway track to connect the two temple towns. The project has received in-principle approval from the state government and includes provisions for a future metro service. Traffic is currently being invited to move elsewhere.

stories.title: Srinagar airport to undergo expansion
stories.summary: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved a 1,677 crore expansion for the civil enclave at Srinagar International Airport. The project includes a new 71,500 square metre terminal designed to handle 10 million passengers annually. The airport has been waiting since 2005 to be international.

stories.title: Odisha to lay foundation for Keonjhar steel plant
stories.summary: Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi announced that the foundation stone for a mega steel plant in Keonjhar will be laid soon. The project is intended to strengthen the district's contribution to a developed India. The plant is currently in the state of being announced.

stories.title: Vizag municipal commissioner transferred
stories.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government transferred GVMC Commissioner Gummalla Srijana following the release of the local election schedule. Srijana, who served as CEO of Visakhapatnam Smart City, previously made headlines for working during the pandemic shortly after childbirth. The government has opted for a change in personnel.

stories.title: Karnataka government meets with Uber
stories.summary: Karnataka Minister Priyank Kharge met with the Uber India team to discuss urban mobility, passenger safety, and regulatory issues. The talks focused on making commuting more efficient for citizens and exploring further engagement between the state and the ride-hailing platform. The meeting was held to discuss future meetings.

stories.title: Italy launches automated solar panel recycling
stories.summary: A new automated line in Sale, Italy, processes up to 120 solar panels per hour using contactless air technology. The facility operates with 94% uptime and three human operators. Italy expects to accumulate 2.2 million tonnes of solar panel waste by 2050, and the machines are ready.

stories.title: Propertymark offers agency toolkit
stories.summary: Propertymark is offering an agency toolkit to help members navigate legal and financial hurdles in the housing market. The association, which has over 19,000 members, aims to help agencies communicate trust to clients. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Pamarawan Island residents build wave barriers
stories.summary: Residents of Pamarawan Island are using bamboo poles and oyster shells to build barriers against rising seas and storm surges. The community has previously elevated homes on concrete layers to combat land subsidence. Nature-based solutions are being deployed where infrastructure has failed to arrive.

stories.title: Machine learning used for urban heat mapping
stories.summary: Researchers have developed a framework integrating machine learning into urban heat island detection and policy planning. The study addresses the difficulty municipal administrations face in translating satellite thermal data into climate-resilient policies. The heat is now being mapped by algorithms.

stories.title: COP31 to feature just transition mechanism
stories.summary: The upcoming COP31 climate summit in Antalya is expected to launch the Belém-Antalya mechanism. The initiative aims to support workers and communities as countries transition away from fossil fuels. The mechanism is currently being established to act as a central hub.

stories.title: Pele Energy Group initiates investigation
stories.summary: Pele Green Energy has initiated an independent investigation into a governance-related matter following a period of rapid growth. The company declined to disclose specific findings but stated the board is considering appropriate action. Entrepreneurial agility has met the requirement for independent oversight.

stories.title: Magaluf regeneration project enters competition
stories.summary: The regeneration of the Torrenova headland in Magaluf has been selected for the EUROPAN 19 architecture competition. The project is a collaboration between the regional government and Calvià City Council. The site is currently waiting for an architect under the age of 40 to redesign it.

stories.title: Architecture students study Azores industrial sites
stories.summary: Students from Laurentian University’s McEwen School of Architecture spent October studying the potential reuse of a former sugar factory and an alcohol factory in the Azores. The project explores how industrial heritage can be preserved for community use. The factories are currently being reimagined.

stories.title: Mavria raises $130 million for data centers
stories.summary: Mavria has raised $130 million to manufacture modular AI data centers in a factory setting. The startup, which launched on November 9, aims to move away from traditional custom-built site construction. The company has achieved a $1 billion valuation on its first day.

stories.title: Project Omega raises $80 million for nuclear fuel recycling
stories.summary: Project Omega has raised $80 million in Series A funding to build nuclear fuel recycling facilities and radioisotope-powered energy systems. The round was led by B Capital with participation from various venture firms. The company is currently focused on expanding its nuclear infrastructure and energy development projects.

stories.title: E8 reports record research project wins
stories.summary: E8, a firm specializing in ontology AI and digital twins, announced it was selected for six national research projects this year. The company plans to provide 3.2 billion won in R&D expenses next year. It described these as the greatest results since its foundation.

stories.title: ProcurePro reaches Startup World Cup finale
stories.summary: Construction tech startup ProcurePro placed in the top 10 at the Startup World Cup in San Francisco. The company, which uses AI to track construction costs, has passed US$10 million in annual recurring revenue. It is now competing for a US$1 million investment prize.

stories.summary: The Design Village, an independent design school in Noida, India, has released a book detailing its founding principles and European campus expansion. Co-authored by Mridu Sahai Patnaik and Paul Hekkert, the text serves as a guide to 21st-century design education and a manifesto for the institution.

stories.summary: The Architectural League of New York has launched the Deborah Norden Travel Fellowship, offering grants for travel projects focused on architecture and landscapes. stories.title: Richmond education firm integrates AI into after-school learning
stories.summary: Building Imagination, a STEAM education organization, is incorporating AI into its after-school programs. The company, founded by a designer and an architect, focuses on activities like virtual tree house building and 3D printing. The founders aim to foster a healthy relationship between children and new technology.

stories.title: MIT architecture project preserves warehouse history
stories.summary: Architect Elizabeth Diller designed the new MIT School of Architecture and Planning space within a century-old storage warehouse. The project aims to keep the building's history alive by exposing its original structure rather than covering it. Diller notes that buildings carry memories of cities and cultures.

research.title: A quantum breakthrough makes light behave like both a solid and a liquid
research.summary: Scientists have observed a bizarre quantum state of matter that combines the structure of a crystal with the frictionless flow of a liquid, all at room temperature. The breakthrough overturns a major practical limitation of exotic quantum experiments and could help bring powerful new light-based computing and sensing.

research.title: Feedback percolation on complex networks
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Traditional percolation theory assumes static microscopic rules, limiting its ability to describe real-world complex systems where macroscopic order actively regulates local interactions. Here, we introduce feedback percolation, an unified framework that dynamically couples the microscopic activation. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Hurricane recovery gaps lie in reconnection, not local restart
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Climate-intensified hurricanes disrupt urban mobility, yet whether recovery is equitable across the rural-urban gradient is unclear. Analyzing device-based mobility for Hurricanes Helene and Milton, we find local activity restarted within approximately 4.5 days in both storms. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
